payload.summary: PLAN_REVIEW round 5 does not converge. Revision 5 closes the prior composite-validator, branded TypeScript, SQL JSON-null, and oversized-BigInt findings; strict OpenSpec, work-package, Python, and TypeScript checks pass. One critical contract blocker remains: Pydantic Literal[1] accepts and normalizes JSON true and 1.0 as schema version 1 while JSON Schema and TypeScript reject them. Two non-blocking consistency nits remain for Unicode maxLength counting in TypeScript and zero identifiers in audit/terminal SQL constraints. External vendor transmission remains unauthorized, so the repository-safe consensus is single-reviewer and lacks cross-vendor quorum.
completed_work: Reviewed commit 75b8d656 and all revision-5 contract, design, spec, task, package, and review artifacts against plan-review-4.
Confirmed the mandatory composite validator, branded TypeScript types, semantic carrier/arithmetic/tracestate checks, SQL JSON type/non-null predicates, and pre-BigInt length cap are present.
Executed the generated Python and TypeScript composite validators against valid, mismatched-carrier, duplicate-tracestate, overflow, and invalid-ID fixtures.
Reproduced that Pydantic accepts schema_version=true and schema_version=1.0 and normalizes both to integer 1 while the other contract surfaces reject them.
Reproduced the JSON-Schema/Python versus JavaScript UTF-16 maxLength disagreement with a 100-code-point astral service name.
Validated the findings schema, strict OpenSpec change, generated TypeScript compilation, work-package schema, dependency references, DAG, lock keys, and git diff whitespace.
Used the repository-safe local reviewer fallback and did not retry prohibited external vendor transmission.

decisions.title: Outcome remains not_converged
decisions.rationale: The version discriminator is the wire-contract selector; accepting boolean/float aliases in one mandatory runtime validator violates the cross-runtime contract and the configured review budget is not exhausted.

decisions.title: Literal equality is not exact JSON type validation
decisions.rationale: Python bool is a subclass of int and Pydantic Literal[1] also accepts 1.0 by equality, so exact type must be checked before model coercion.

next_steps: PLAN_FIX: add an exact-type before-validator for schema_version to every versioned Pydantic wire model and freeze true/1.0/string negative fixtures across all runtime surfaces.
PLAN_FIX: use Unicode code-point counts in TypeScript bounded-string checks or constrain identifier grammars to ASCII in every contract.
PLAN_FIX: reject all-zero W3C IDs consistently in audit and terminal SQL constraints.
Re-run PLAN_REVIEW using the repository-safe local fallback unless external vendor transmission is explicitly authorized.
